speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We have seen the law take effect since.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Companies submitted their first reports for the Mandatory Packaging Reporting scheme last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We see the first fruits of our shift from a linear take-make-throw economy to a circular one, where waste is turned into resources to be put to good use again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030 two years ago, with a comprehensive national agenda for sustainable development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Last year, we raised our national climate target to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, affirming Singapore's strong commitment to climate action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To move decisively towards this goal, we passed the Carbon Pricing (Amendment) Bill to ensure our carbon pricing regime supports the transition to a low-carbon future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These measures are also intended to spark behaviour change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: They are a call for everyone to act, to participate and take a stake in Singapore's zero-waste journey to shift from a throwaway culture towards a more sustainable paradigm, one that is characterised by mindful consumption and the sustainable habits of reducing, reusing and recycling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: So, I would like to take some time to explain Singapore's approach towards plastics and plastic pollution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Plastics, which are made from non-renewable fossil fuels, contribute to our carbon emissions when they are produced, transported and incinerated at end-of-life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Plastic pollution, especially in the form of transboundary marine litter, is a global problem, spoiling our environment and causing harm to wildlife.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Curbing our use of plastics would protect our environment and conserve finite resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: However, plastics, including single-use plastics, have many important uses and continue to be an essential aspect in many aspects of our daily lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For example, it is a key component in personal protective equipment and disposable masks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Many Singaporeans also use plastic bags to dispose of trash hygienically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The littering, wasteful use and unnecessary disposal of plastics are.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: While we share a common global problem of plastic pollution, we do not necessarily share a common solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Every country has a different context, characterised by unique circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Many countries are plagued by indiscriminate littering of plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Inadequate or poorly maintained waste disposal facilities can also cause plastics to leak into the environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In Singapore, our strong stance against littering, along with an effective waste management system, has limited the leakage of plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Likewise, because plastics can persist in the environment for many years if they are directly landfilled, some countries are introducing regulations to ban or restrict single-use plastics, and companies are responding by switching to biodegradable substitutes like paper, biodegradable plastics or wood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: However, biodegradable materials do not offer the same incremental benefit in Singapore, where all incinerable waste is not directly landfilled, but is either recycled or properly disposed of at waste-to-energy plants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In addition, every material type requires precious resources, like water, energy, fossil fuels and trees, for their production, transportation and disposal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: All these materials also leave behind a carbon footprint.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Hence, the most effective way to reduce our environmental impact is to reduce our use of all types of materials, not just plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Where we cannot eliminate the use of materials, we need to find effective ways of aggregating them for recycling where possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is where the Resource Sustainability (Amendment) Bill comes in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With the disposable carrier bag charge, we hope to nudge Singaporeans to reduce their use of disposable carrier bags, including plastic bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With the beverage container return scheme, we will put in place a better system to extract clean and valuable streams of plastic and metal recyclables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The disposable carrier bag charge is, first and foremost, a behavioural nudge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Disposable carrier bags will remain available at retail establishments, but making the cost of the bag visible in supermarkets prompts us to pause and consider how many we really need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It is a reminder to bring our own reusable bags and to reduce the use of disposables – an essential feature of sustainable living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The charge was a recommendation of a 2020 Citizens’ Workgroup, and we have engaged the public and supermarket operators extensively on the policy details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Under section 23F, a registered retailer will be required to charge a minimum of five cents per bag provided to customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Registered retailers may apply to be deregistered if their annual turnover does not exceed $100 million for each of three consecutive years, or if they are no longer a regulated retailer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Section 23H will require registered retailers to communicate this charge to their customers and set it out separately in receipts where provided.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To monitor compliance, section 23I will require registered retailers to report data to the National Environment Agency (NEA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For public accountability and transparency on the use of proceeds, section 23K will require registered retailers to publish information on the number of bags issued, the amount of proceeds collected and how the proceeds were used.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Bill will also give effect to a beverage container return scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is an extended producer responsibility scheme, where producers are made responsible for the collection and recycling of beverage containers like plastic bottles and metal cans that they put on the market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Producers, typically, rely on a scheme operator to carry out these responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: A deposit will be collected for each beverage product covered by the scheme, or "covered beverage product", and refunded fully when empty beverage containers are returned at designated return points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: While the scheme is well-established in many jurisdictions around the world, it is the first in Southeast Asia and one of the first few in Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The scheme will be a pathfinder for Singapore in our move towards a circular economy, especially for plastics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Singapore's recycling rate for plastics is low, at only 6%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The scheme will aggregate a stream of clean and high-quality plastic and metal recyclables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The plastic bottles collected will comprise mostly PET, or polyethylene terephthalate, a valuable fraction that is highly sought-after by companies looking to use a higher proportion of recycled PET, or rPET, in their containers to fulfil their sustainability commitments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This rPET can be manufactured into new containers, breathing life into the circular model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The beverage container return scheme was a recommendation of a 2019 Citizens’ Workgroup.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To design a scheme suitable for Singapore, my Ministry and NEA conducted over two years of engagements with stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: I announced at the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment's (MSE's) Committee of Supply (COS) debates that the scheme will cover plastic bottles and metal cans with volumes ranging from 150 millimetres to three litres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will move progressively towards this and set a return rate target of 60% and 70% in the first and second year respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This amount takes into account public feedback, as well as the experience of other jurisdictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In a recent REACH public consultation, the majority of respondents, about 84%, indicated that a deposit amount of 10 cents or higher would be suitable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: A higher deposit would encourage participation and a higher return rate, but we do not want the deposit to be too high such that it deters purchases of pre-packaged beverages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Hence, on balance, we determined that a 10-cent deposit per container would suffice to help achieve an 80% return-rate target.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To ensure a robust return point network, Singapore Food Agency (SFA)-licensed supermarkets with a floor area of more than 200 square metres, which comprises about 400 supermarkets, will be required to set up return points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Supermarkets are ideal for this role, as they are major sales channels of beverages and preferred by respondents in our public consultations as return point locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This approach of deploying return points at supermarkets is proven to be efficient and associated with high return rates in overseas jurisdictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To enhance convenience and encourage consumer participation, we will also work with the scheme operator and other stakeholders to establish additional return points in other accessible locations in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To give effect to the scheme, we will introduce a new Part 4B.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Section 23O will require all producers, that is, importers and manufacturers of covered beverage products, to join the licensed scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Section 23P will require containers of covered beverage products to be labelled: first, with a deposit mark for customers to identify covered beverage products; and second, with a barcode to facilitate the acceptance of empty beverage containers at return points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Section 23Q makes it clear that the deposit is not part of the price of the beverage product.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The beverage container or the use of the beverage container, is, therefore, not subject to the Goods and Services Tax.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The deposit, which is first provided by the producer to the scheme operator under section 23R, must be collected by every supplier for each covered beverage product the supplier sells.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Section 23S mandates that certain persons must set up return points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Section 23U requires return point operators to refund the deposit when an empty beverage container is returned, except under certain circumstances, such as if the deposit mark or barcode is so damaged that it cannot be read or scanned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will also be amending Part 6 of the RSA, which provides for the licensing of the producer responsibility scheme operator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For the beverage container return scheme, a not-for-profit, industry-led scheme operator is preferred.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is similar to successful schemes in other jurisdictions, such as Norway and Denmark.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: As the scheme is owned and run by the industry, the scheme operator will be able to tap on the industry’s capabilities and resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It will also have a strong incentive to operate it efficiently and effectively, to keep scheme costs low for all parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: My Ministry and NEA will continue to engage industry players on the appointment of a suitable scheme operator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: More details will be announced in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The scheme operator will be licensed under the existing Part 6, with a few additions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: There is a need to safeguard the interests of various stakeholders, for example, if the scheme operator is led by larger producers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: A new section 29A will enable the Minister to prescribe requirements for up to one-third of the scheme operator's key appointment holders, and to require the scheme operator to obtain NEA's approval for these key appointments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Additional safeguards will be introduced, under section 32, to ensure that the power to impose financial penalties is exercised appropriately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA, in determining the amount of financial penalty, will be required to consider a list of factors, such as the nature, gravity and duration of the non-compliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We have been engaging the industry closely on the details of the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The beverage producers who have expressed interest to jointly support the formation of the scheme operator are seriously looking at implementation details, such as setting up return points and the printing of the deposit mark and barcode for beverage containers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: While we want to move quickly to facilitate a shift towards a more sustainable way of doing business, we understand that the industry needs time to plan and set up a robust and effective scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Thereafter, a grace period of three months will be provided for the beverage and retail industry to clear unlabelled stock, which will not carry a deposit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will continue to support and engage the industry as they work to fulfil their obligations under the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Prior to the commencement date, we will also work with the appointed scheme operator on education and outreach efforts to prepare consumers and other stakeholders for the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We are also building on earlier foundations laid in the RSA to close the food waste loop.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Food waste is a priority waste stream due to its high generation and low recycling rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: When food is wasted, so are all the resources used to cultivate, process and prepare it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With growing pressures on food supply chains and resource availability, we must rethink wasteful linear models and capture value from food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To promote resource recovery for food waste, we introduced segregation and treatment requirements in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The requirements are intended to apply to industrial and commercial buildings, such as hotels, shopping malls and factories, which are large generators of food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In addition to facilitating the treatment or conversion of food waste into useful products, such as new food products or animal feed, other benefits include reduction in disamenities, such as odour and pest nuisance, at the premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We are also investing in critical infrastructure to ensure sufficient food waste treatment capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Construction of the food waste treatment facility at Tuas Nexus is ongoing and forms part of our efforts to support the industry in treating the segregated food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To complement segregation and treatment requirements, we will be introducing a new requirement for building managers to submit food waste reports to the NEA under section 27C.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will raise awareness on the amount of food waste generated and encourage building managers to pursue waste minimisation opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To ensure minimal burden on building managers, we have simplified data requirements to key information, such as the overall building-level tonnages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In the long run, reducing food waste and segregating food waste for treatment could also reduce costs for businesses, such as by reducing waste disposal costs downstream and reaping value from transforming food waste into higher value products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will stagger the implementation of the food waste segregation, treatment and reporting requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: These are buildings for which application for planning approval was submitted on or after 1 January 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Part 5 of the RSA, which has not yet come into force, will be repealed and re-enacted to allow for the staggered implementation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With more circular production practices emerging, there are increasing possibilities to transform food waste into higher-value products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For example, waste bread can be used to make beverages and spent grains from breweries can be processed into powder to be used as ingredients for food products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Therefore, our revised regulatory framework will also provide flexibility to enable the pursuit of these innovative food waste treatment methods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Under the original Part 5, building managers of new buildings must cause segregated food waste to be treated onsite.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Under the original Part 5, building occupiers of both new and existing buildings must use the segregation and treatment arrangements provided by their building managers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In assessing whether approval will be granted, NEA will take into consideration if the proposed treatment methods process food waste into higher-value products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: At its core, the issue of waste stems from human actions and choices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Likewise, the ultimate solution to achieve zero waste and a circular economy lies not in regulations or technologies, but with us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: With the Resource Sustainability (Amendment) Bill, we are putting in place stronger measures for individuals and the private sector to reduce waste and recycle more to achieve circularity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: But these measures are merely a means to an end.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The goal for these initiatives must be to catalyse a change that extends beyond the boundaries of the initiatives themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: They must cultivate new behaviours and encourage a sustainable way of life amongst Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The amendments to the RSA will help to get everyone to pitch in for sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The private sector will need to establish circular business models to properly collect and treat their beverage products at end-of-life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Building managers and occupiers will need to track the amount of food waste generated and provide space to segregate food waste for treatment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: As individuals and consumers, we will need to rinse and segregate empty beverage containers so that we can return them for recycling and a refund of our deposit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will also need to remember to bring our shopping bags when leaving the house.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: But we will make this shift knowing that it is the right thing to do, that it is good for the environment and for future generations, and so that we can take pride in the stewardship of our resources and our country and do our part in our global fight against plastic pollution and climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Our journey towards zero waste will not be easy, but I can say with every confidence that it will be a rewarding one.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: However, the purpose of these new policies must do more than reflect a message of global warming.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: These polices must address the need to make small but impactful adjustments to our daily habits.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Let us talk about disposable plastic carrier bags.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: In some of these places, plastic bag bans have not been as effective.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Like in California, studies have shown that while shoppers used fewer plastic bags, the sales and utilisation of trash bags has proportionally increased.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: A migrant domestic helper, Ms Maricel Vicente from Bacarra, a municipality in the province of Ilocos Norte in the Philippines, shared with me that in her hometown, the supermarkets over there do not provide plastic bags, styrofoam or any plastic containers.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: They only provide thin brown bags, with no handles.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: These bags are not helpful if you have to store and carry your groceries.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The inconvenience reminded the shoppers to bring their own reusable shopping bags.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Having said that, the additional five cents to each shopper will probably not deter most of them from the usage of plastic bags.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We should practice what supermarkets in Bacarra does.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Completely stop providing plastic bags and encourage shoppers to bring their own recyclable shopping bags.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Should shoppers require a bag for their groceries, they can always purchase recyclable bags just like any other product sold at the premises.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Should bags be required for trash, trash bags can always be purchased at the supermarket.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This way, we are all implementing simple changes to slow down global warming.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: To add, this will also avoid any profiteering from the sale of plastic bags that was once provided free of charge.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Let us talk about the beverage container return scheme.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We should do more to encourage this campaign by creating new roles.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Maybe we could support the seniors, who once collected discarded metal cans to be sold.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Alternatively, scheme operators can hire seniors to manage the collection stations.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: However, for these schemes to succeed, attention to details in their implementation is key and nothing beats the importance of communicating public education intensively.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I will start with the plastic bag charge.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I had mentioned that Taiwan had just, then, announced a blanket ban in single-use plastics, including straws, cups and shopping bags, by 2030.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Prior to that, there was a progressive plan to make people pay for plastic products like plastic bags, straws, disposable food containers and disposable utensils in the interim.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Back then, there was already more than 40 countries taxing or limiting the use of plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The evidence had shown that even modest policy interventions can have significant impact.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I repeated this call in my Budget debate speech in 2021.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I, therefore, welcome the imposition of a plastic bag charge to be formally included under today's amendment of the Resource Sustainability Act.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I am also heartened that Senior Minister of State Amy Khor recently cited statistics in Hong Kong, Taiwan and the United Kingdom (UK), where after the introduction of a plastic bag charge in those countries, their usage of plastic carrier bags fell.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I quoted the example of the UK in this House five years ago.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I am glad that the Government accepted the recommendations of the Citizens' Workgroup on Reducing Excessive Consumption of Disposables to impose a plastic bag charge.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This nudging is extremely important as we are talking about the long-term habits of individuals.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In 2018, in response to my call for a plastic bag charge in comparison with other countries like Taiwan and the UK, Senior Minister of State Amy Khor said, "Miss Cheng Li Hui and Mr Dennis Tan asked about our efforts to deal with plastic waste and, specifically, whether we will impose a charge or ban on single-use plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Unlike many of the countries that have imposed a ban or mandatory charge on plastic bags, we do not directly landfill our plastic disposables but incinerate them.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Hence, we do not face the land and water pollution issues that plague those countries.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Plastic bags are also necessary for responsible and hygienic bagging of waste in our moist, tropical climate.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Unbagged household waste attracts pests like cockroaches and rats, creating serious environmental and health problems." She also said that, "There are actually good reasons that single-use plastic bags have to be given or used by the public for bagging their waste.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Therefore, the issue is really about excessive use – not that you cannot use plastic bags, but excessive use of plastic bags." I agreed with her, then and now, that plastic bags are needed for the bagging of waste and that the issue is about excessive use of plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I also thought, then and now, that the fact that we incinerate our rubbish does not remove the need to educate and persuade Singaporeans to try to reduce our plastic bag consumption and to consider greater measures to reduce the use of plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Hence, my suggestion for a plastic bag charge back in 2018.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In 2020, I said in my Budget debate speech that mindsets must shift in the way we consume – to only use what we need to use.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: For single-use plastic bags, I had asked – can we take or use what we really need?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can we pack more things into each plastic bag?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Do we really need to double-bag all our groceries at the checkouts?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If we only need to use, say, one or two plastic bags for very few disposals a day, do we need to take 20 bags from the supermarket in a week?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We can also reduce the number of single-use plastic bags we need to take for our refuse, by concurrently using good quality reusable shopping bags.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We may end up using fewer plastic bags and may still have enough bags for our refuse.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In my 2021 COS debate cut for MSE, I reiterated my call for mindsets to shift in the way we consume, to only use what we need to use and called for less use of plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Indeed, while the plastic bag charge will certainly nudge behaviours when people feel the pinch of having to pay for plastic bags, what is more important, I feel, is that we must get all Singaporeans to understand fully: why we are doing this; why we need to reduce plastic bag use; how we can reduce plastic bag production; how we should reduce the number of plastic bags we incinerate every day; and, most of all, to internalise them in our minds so that they instinctively guide our everyday actions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have been using such bags for supermarket shopping for many years – a habit I first had when I was a student abroad.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In my 2021 COS debate cut for MSE, I reiterated the call to use more good quality reusable shopping bags in supermarkets or retail shops.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Last year, our Aljunied-Hougang Town Council gave a reusable shopping bag to each of the Housing and Development Board (HDB) households in Aljunied and Hougang Town.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope it will be a useful reminder to our residents to use more good reusable bags and minimise the use of plastic bags.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We have come a long way, even in the last few years, but I hope that, with the plastic bag charge, mindsets will change for those who are used to taking many plastic bags at the supermarket.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We need to remind ourselves to only take what we absolutely need.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can the Government share its staged plans, if any, to extend the plastic bag charge beyond its current category of retailers of more than $100 million turnover?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I support this scheme and I think it can significantly reduce the amount of plastic bottles and metal cans, which are currently being disposed of instead of being deliberately recycled via recycling bins and other proper ways.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: When we are out, there may not always be a recycling bin in sight when we want to dispose of our drink can or bottle after we have consumed the beverage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I can imagine the number of bottles or cans which are thrown into normal rubbish bins every day and taken to our refuse incinerator.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Also, although many Singaporeans have developed good recycling habits or practices, many are still not doing so.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Singapore is not even at the stage as some first-world countries are where households are required to segregate their waste in different categories, such as general waste, paper, plastic, glass, metal, and so on.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We are using one recycling bin for different waste but, sadly, it is a common sight to see general waste and contaminated materials being thrown into recycling bins.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I believe that the beverage return scheme will minimise wrongful disposal, encourage more recycling and inculcate better recycling habits.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Like the plastic bag charge, the beverage container return scheme is, sadly, a form of enforced public education.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: But it will bring certain knowledge to those who are hitherto ignorant or indifferent to recycling.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This is important as it complements retail outlets at venues where the beverage containers can be returned.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope to see a significant reduction in the volume of such waste being sent to our incinerators after the beverage container return scheme and the plastic bag charge scheme are introduced.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I also look forward to the scheme being extended to glass and beverage cartons soon.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Before I leave this point, and as a follow-up to my COS cut in 2018 on a similar topic, I am also going to ask the Minister for an update on the Government's plans, if any, to reduce the use of styrofoam food and beverage containers, which are still widely used.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: When I was a little boy, I remember being reminded by my parents to finish every bit of food on my plate and being told off for wasting food.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Some of us will remember being told by our parents that we have to finish every single grain of rice in our bowl.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: It is important to curb food wastage because other resources have been invested to grow the food ingredients as well as the cooking of the ingredients for consumption.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: According to the United Nations Environment Programme's (UNEP's) Food Waste Index Report 2021, 17% of our food ends up being wasted in retail and by consumers, particularly in households.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Further, food waste has grown by 20% in the past decade in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: According to UNEP's Executive Director, Mr Inger Andersen, each person is said to waste an average of 74 kilogrammes of food every year in all the middle- and high-income countries in the world.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: According to UNEP, 8% to 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions are associated with food that is not consumed.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Wasted food meant wasted efforts and resources in producing them, including land, fertilisers, water, packaging, transportation, fuel and so on.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Food waste may also be deposited in landfills, increasing the production of methane emissions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Even in Singapore, where we burn our waste before depositing in landfill, cutting down waste food will also greatly reduce the amount of waste we incinerate and, to some extent, ultimately dumped in landfills.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Reducing food waste will also be of great help in making our progress towards our climate goals, including our 2030 emission targets.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: That brings us to why we need to do food waste segregation and reporting.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Segregation and reporting are the first step to help us to realise and account for our food waste.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: A retailer or food service provider can, accordingly, be better guided to take actions to reduce food waste and/or even direct food waste to better mitigation measures.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Unsold or unconsumed food can be passed on to food banks and charities for consumption by the less privileged.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They can also be converted to composts, animal feed or biofuel gases as they are being done in other countries.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Achieving this target would have significant implications for the fight against climate change.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: UNEP's Food Waste Index Report supports the goals of SDG 12.3, with its comprehensive and reliable food waste data collection, analysis and modelling to date; and helping countries to measure food waste at household, food service and retail levels; to track national progress towards 2030 and to report on SDG target of 12.3.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I support the proposed amendments in this Bill for food waste segregation and reporting, which will complement and support global efforts via UNEP and FAO and through the Food Waste Index Report.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Naturally, Singapore, Singaporeans and our Government must do our part to support with clear actions the SDG target of 12.3.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: UNEP has reported that the true scale of food waste and its impacts have not been well-understood, until now.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I would argue that we really should educate Singaporeans of all ages and educational levels on the perils of food waste and how we must reduce food waste and channel produced food resources to better uses in mitigation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: While our Government has through its Zero Waste Masterplan and the guides it produced for F&B outlets, supermarkets and food manufacturers to guide and help businesses to reduce food waste – with greater focus on production processes, proper inventory management and effective perishables handling – more must be done to educate domestic households and individuals so that every Singaporean knows about the issue of food wastage and how every Singaporean can consciously minimise food wastage in our daily living habits.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I applaud many different organisations like Food Bank, Willing Hearts, many lesser known or less formally organised groups and Singaporeans who are already doing that, such as the Red Collective and the many food rescue groups operating in different parts of Singapore, bringing excess food to lower-income Singaporeans, reducing food wastage and helping the food-insecured Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I also hope that the beverage container return scheme will soon be extended to glass bottles and beverage cartons.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Although Singapore has a small global footprint, our globalised economy will influence and shape the wider commercial networks beyond our shores.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Within our shores, we are already facing the environmental impact.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: For example, the Lorong Halus dumping ground, a 234-hectare landfill, was opened in the 1970s.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: For many years, it was plagued by illegal dumping, foul smell and pollution of the surrounding natural habitat.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Therefore, we will need to develop more capacity beyond Pulau Semakau.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Of which, about 820 million are plastic bags from supermarkets and close to half a billion PET bottles and disposable plastic items.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: These plastic products require massive energy and resources to manufacture, distribute and dispose of.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Some studies mentioned that Singapore only recycles 13% of domestic waste.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Most were due to the leakage of food and liquid waste, as well as e-waste and styrofoam, which contributed to most of the contamination, rendering most items unsuitable for recycling.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: When I engage businesses, youths and residents, many have expressed passion for the climate emergency and their desire to play a more active role.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: As individuals, they want to have more alternatives and access to participate in more sustainable activities and lifestyles.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: As a citizen, they urged for more action, a swifter and deliberate effort to push toward a more sustainable society.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: In addition, I hear the youths actively advocating for more action to secure their future and our future generations.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: This Bill will enable us to reduce waste generation and recover valuable materials from crucial waste elements.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: It will allow us to divert waste from Semakau and extend its lifespan.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: The reduced waste generation will reduce our carbon emissions from incineration, build capabilities and move towards a more circular economy.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: I have a few questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Will this be aggregated at the group or subsidiary level?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share more on the reporting and recording-keeping requirements and how often should these retailers report the details of the bag charge requirements, and if there are any baseline requirements on how this should be published?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Will there be a future mandatory requirement to channel the collected proceeds to support social and environmental causes?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: On the beverage container return scheme, in the scenario where the scheme operators have failed to achieve the required return rate, what will be the consequences and mitigating factors?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: How will the disposal and collection scheme work when cross-border commercial activities are involved, such as F&B services onboard aircrafts and ships?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: On food waste reporting, what are the approval considerations for new building managers to pursue alternative food waste treatment methods located off-site?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have been speaking up for a charge on single-use carrier bags since 2016.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad we are finally debating this Bill in this House today.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I support this Bill, as all the initiatives will encourage greener habits, reduce waste and extend the lifespan of our landfill at Pulau Semakau.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is a point that I have been stressing repeatedly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is on the expansion of the disposable carrier bag charge to more, if not all, retail businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We currently only apply the charge to large supermarkets because they have the resources to implement it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know we want to start small and slow and give time for the industry to adapt.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But if we want to change mindsets and slash the use of single-use bags, we need to eventually expand the charge to all retail businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A longer-term roadmap gives businesses time to adapt their business models and change their systems.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With enough notice, some businesses may even pre-empt the rules and impose their own bag charge before the regulations come into force.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on applying the charge to online purchases.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Increasingly common are "click and collect" purchases, where customers shop online and collect their products at a physical store.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Since products are bought in advance, customers can make plans to bring their own reusable bags to collect their purchases.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How will the charge be determined during check-out online?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, will the Senior Minister of State consider implementing the disposable bag charge for online deliveries?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Grocery deliveries, in particular, are notorious for being packed in layers upon layers of disposable bags.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Online grocers are eroding the market share of brick-and-mortar supermarkets and we should be looking at seriously reducing the waste they generate as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third point is on the beverage container return scheme.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the scheme, customers have to pay a small deposit for certain pre-packaged drinks, which will be refunded when they return the container for recycling.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will encourage consumers to return beverage containers and increase their recycling rate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, this may erode the income of those who collect cans for a living.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If so, what additional support will be extended to them?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My fourth and final point relates to the new requirement for building managers to report on food waste being segregated and treated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While treatment of food waste is a good way to reduce the impact of excess food, it would be even better if we can donate excess food instead.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that we are doing more to tackle food waste and I am glad to share that the Good Samaritans Committee is making good progress in drafting the Good Samaritans Food Donation Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This proposed law will help allay concerns about liability issues from the donation of food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It will help reduce food waste further and also provide food for the hungry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are doing further consultations with stakeholders and I hope to introduce this Bill in Parliament through a Private Member's Bill soon.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Obviously, the cost of the bags has already been priced in and bundled with the selling prices of the products for sale.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With the implementation of the disposable carrier bag charge, how would the Ministry ensure that the participating businesses pass on the cost savings from the plastic bags to consumers?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to ask what would be the estimated amount of carbon reduction derived from the decreased production of bags, in addition to the environmental impact, especially the harm caused to marine life.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What is the possibility of getting supermarkets and other stores to switch to alternatives, such as biodegradable bags?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry work with retailers and supermarkets to increase the availability of such bags?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As for beverage containers, I would like to ask how the Ministry will ensure that return points for the containers are easily accessible beyond supermarkets.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I support making it compulsory for supermarkets to have collection points as many people buy their drinks from there.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is the only way to ensure that our efforts to tackle plastic bag problems will be sustainable over the long term.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If we do not provide reasonable alternatives, we are simply pushing the problem of people obtaining plastic bags from supermarkets to other sources.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many residents ask me how they can bag their rubbish going forward as they find five cents per bag pretty expensive.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Surely, we do not want residents throwing their rubbish, especially food waste, directly into the rubbish chutes, in order to save on the cost of bags.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   One challenge is the issue of the proper bagging of waste, especially food waste, before disposal.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If we do not provide a reasonable alternative, we are simply pushing the problem of people obtaining plastic bags from supermarkets to other sources.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many residents ask me how they can bag their rubbish going forward, as they find five cents per bag quite expensive.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Surely, we do not want residents throwing their rubbish, especially food waste, directly into the rubbish chutes, in order to save on the cost of bags.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will also help to close the food waste loop in Singapore, even for households.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will the Ministry be implementing initiatives similar to the Bloobox?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such products can be launched on a wide scale through supermarkets and wet markets.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Countries, such as Kenya, Rwanda and our neighbour, Thailand, have introduced stringent rules on the production and usage of plastic bags.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Kenya, in particular, has implemented what has been called "the world's strictest plastic ban" and banned all single-use plastic bags throughout the country.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Three years after they did so, some of their national parks began disallowing all single-use plastics on the premises.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Although they did this primarily to tackle the littering problem, they have also successfully reduced plastic waste.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that the measures this House is debating are merely the start towards our equally ambitious measures.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Reducing use of plastic bags in brick-and-mortar businesses is an excellent start and I hope MSE can go beyond by also looking into the online retail space.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Since the pandemic, many more have been shopping online.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Merchants from e-commerce platforms are especially generous with their packaging, often using layers of bubble wrap and other materials.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Sometimes, we find our items to be very small, but the boxes to be very big.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Granted, retailers do so to ensure that products are delivered in good condition to their buyers and we can hardly fault them for that.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: But there is a massive amount of packaging involved in these shipments and deliveries.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It is heartening to know that some companies in the private sector are already initiating efforts to reduce and reuse packaging.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Government accelerate these efforts by introducing a "sustainable packaging" mark?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: This mark would indicate to online customers that the packaging used by merchants is either second-hand, compostable or otherwise recycled and, therefore, eco-friendly.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We can work with packaging companies and environmental groups to co-create the minimum sustainability standards that packaging materials should adhere to in order to earn this mark.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: We can also work with online retail aggregating platforms like Alibaba Express, Taobao, Lazada and Shopee to enrol online retail consumers to rate retailers on their packaging practices.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Such a mark will create collaboration between consumers and online retailers to achieve greener online shopping together.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: By exercising their purchasing choices in favour of retailers who use second-hand packaging, it will incentivise merchants to adopt less wasteful packaging practices.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: In a study by Ipsos last year, 88% of Singaporeans said they were receptive to donating used packaging and 62% of Singaporeans said they were receptive to receiving their products in second-hand packaging – myself included.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: However, merchants are reluctant to adopt second-hand packaging due to the low cost and easy availability of packaging products – what we call "virgin packaging".

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Some people may resist this, as the concern is that, merchants will transfer the cost to consumers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: However, I do not necessarily see that as a bad thing as it will provide a disincentive for excessive shopping and make consumers more deliberative and conscious about what they are buying and to differentiate between things that are nice to have but not really necessary and reduce wasteful consumption as a whole.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: If we were to implement these measures, the Government should work towards the necessary infrastructure enablement to ensure a coordinated system of localised facilities to collect and reuse packaging.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: It is important that we help merchants with changing their practices to make it as seamless and pain-free as we can.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, it is important that the scheme to charge for disposable plastic bags has been carefully studied for implementation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To ensure the success of this policy, we should learn from the experiences of other countries that have implemented similar policies.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What are some of the challenges that they have faced?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What are the key lessons that we can learn from them?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have received feedback from residents who questioned the need to discourage the use of plastic bags at supermarkets.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They argue that these bags are often reused by households to bag rubbish.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They have expressed concern that discouraging plastic bag use may result in food waste being thrown directly down rubbish chutes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This leads to other environmental issues, such as the breeding of pests.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans in place to monitor this situation?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be increased enforcement of regulations targeting the failure to properly bag rubbish for disposal?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Ministry has assured that the public will continue to have access to disposable bags from other sources.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This includes those available for bagging fresh produce from supermarkets.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Hence, it should not hinder the practice of responsible waste disposal.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Even so, this could lead residents to exploit such loopholes by taking extra bags.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some residents have also shared that since plastic is incinerated in Singapore, their remains take up less space in landfills than other types of waste.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They felt that the resources spent on discouraging the use of plastic bags could be better spent on managing other types of waste instead.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Moreover, while the plastic bag charge is a positive step, it should not be viewed as the ultimate solution.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Consumers might start purchasing single-use plastic bags from online and overseas retailers, where they are usually more affordable in bulk.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry tackle this problem and ensure that we are not simply redirecting residents to another source of plastic bags that cannot be recycled?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This may cause our residents to pay more, and it will not solve the problem.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will this not impact our less well-off residents?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Another concern regarding the plastic bag charge is that retailers may use their voluntary participation in the scheme as an excuse to incorporate the cost into the prices of their products.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In doing so, they continue to give out plastic bags without offering consumers a choice.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This would make it difficult for consumers to know that they are paying for the bags as the charge would be factored into the total bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Whilst this may be small and insignificant when compared to the overall cost of the sales, this may constitute profiteering, especially for those who may have brought their own bags.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is critical to grant all consumers the freedom to make choices about plastic bag use to achieve the policy's objective.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Otherwise, some businesses may take advantage of the situation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Is the five-cent charge per plastic bag enough to discourage consumption or should we consider charging more?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In fact, some retailers are already charging 10 cents per bag.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I understand that supermarkets will be required to publish information on how the proceeds from the sale of plastic bags would be used for charitable or other environmental causes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there existing guidelines as to what constitutes proper use of the funds?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Next, we should also consider expanding the plastic bag charge to cover all single-use disposable plastic items.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My colleagues and I have raised concerns about the environmental impact of such items in Parliament before and I have asked about the measures to reduce their use by enterprises.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: With meetings, gatherings and events resuming in full force, disposable cutlery, plates and cups are, once again, being used at these occasions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For individuals, many food and beverages (F&B) retailers are already charging for takeaways with disposable containers and single-use cutlery.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, a mandatory charge for disposable items would not be a new concept.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am of the view that charging for single-use plastic bags is the right step forward as we should discourage waste.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Perhaps, when we, as a society, better understand the detrimental impact of plastic pollution on our health and the environment, we may consider a complete ban on single-use plastics as momentary convenience may lead to prolonged harm on our health and on the environment.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, I wish to raise some concerns regarding the beverage container return scheme.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there any potential disruptions in the waste management industry that need to be addressed, especially for elderly waste collectors who rely on collecting recyclables to supplement their income?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Ministry mandate the establishment of beverage container return points in the community and in public areas instead of leaving it as a voluntary initiative?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It seems reasonable to assume that these return points would be more heavily used, given that many consumers would purchase their beverages online or from heartland retailers, vending machines and supermarkets.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These individuals would have to incur the extra costs of beverages but may be unable to return the beverage containers for a refund of their deposits.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What measures are in place to engage the public and ensure a high level of awareness and participation rates, particularly during the initial stages of implementation?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the campaign be promoted in schools and at community events?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will there be publicity materials in stores and public areas, reminding and instructing consumers to utilise the return points?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, I have some questions regarding the food waste management scheme.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Locations which come to mind are the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) cookhouses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Other potential sites may include schools, hospitals and nursing homes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: With on-site classes returning in full force, have there been any recent studies conducted on the amount of food waste generated in these premises?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This may serve as an opportunity to raise awareness among National Service recruits and students about the importance of not wasting food.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is important to start educating individuals from a young age.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I note that under current provisions, new buildings must treat food waste on-site.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
