text: However, with approval from the National Environment Agency (NEA), building managers of new buildings may seek alternative food waste treatment methods located off-site.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If so, how does the Ministry define whether an off-site facility is adequately close to the buildings to ensure efficient and safe transportation of food waste?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Pursuing these initiatives is, ultimately, about balancing business costs and sustainability efforts.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Nonetheless, this does not need to be a zero-sum game.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: More innovative solutions and technology must be explored to make going green less costly and reduce the associated overheads.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Most importantly, we should endeavour not to have waste at all.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We must embrace a culture that minimises waste or, even better, no waste, and practises consumption in moderation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This cannot be the sole responsibility of the Government.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Rather, it must be a collective effort of every individual and organisation to make a significant impact on our environment.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A New England proverb puts it most succinctly on how we can do so, "Use it up, wear it out, make it do, or do without." By doing this, we can achieve a greener and more sustainable Singapore for every one.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are, understandably, concerned about higher costs as a result of the new legislation.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Allow me to share some of their specific queries.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does this charge apply to convenience stores like Cheers and 7-Eleven, which are related to the NTUC Fairprice and Dairy Farm groups respectively?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   About 80% of our residents' households live in Housing and Development Board and about 16% in condominiums.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is a habit for Singaporeans to put their rubbish into plastic bags before throwing them down the rubbish chutes.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am concerned that residents will proceed to buy more plastic bags, which may be cheaper than five cents per piece if they buy in bulk.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Unfortunately, there seems to be no better material than plastic to bag wet and perishable products.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): I am also concerned that reusable plastic bags, which shoppers are encouraged to bring along, may not be environmentally friendlier if the frequency of usage is low.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would also like to ask how much space does a single returning point take up, and what would be the estimated monthly cost to operate a returning point?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry ascertain the success of this scheme?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Will the scheme be funded by taxpayers' money?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are there any Government grants that the beverage producers can tap upon to minimise producer fees which may be passed on to consumers eventually?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am worried that consumers will likely end up paying more if the recycled material value is lower than the cost of joining and complying with the licensed scheme.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The other concern would be over people fighting over used metal cans and plastic bottles at F&B joints or rubbish collection points.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are food waste generators required to report the amount of food waste periodically?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, the disposable carrier bag charge or "bag charge".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am glad that many Members have expressed support for the bag charge, including Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Louis Ng.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, many Members, including Miss Cheng Li Hui, former Member of Parliament, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah as well as non-governmental organisations like Zero Waste SG and WWF Singapore have also called for a charge on disposable bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Louis Ng, as he noted, has been speaking up about a charge since 2016 and I commend him for his persistence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government has been studying the experiences of other jurisdictions that have implemented a bag charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are also mindful of our local circumstances, where plastic bags are widely used by households to dispose of waste hygienically and where incinerable waste is not directly landfilled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We convened the Citizens' Workgroup in 2020 to tap into diverse views and insights to address the issues of disposables.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: After we accepted the recommendation to implement a disposable carrier bag charge, we consulted widely to hear different considerations, seek feedback and build collective support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am glad that Mr Dennis Tan agrees that it is the excessive use of disposables that we need to tackle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: By placing a visible cost on each bag, we will be more sensitive to the impact of our consumption on the environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While Ms Joan Pereira raised concerns about cost, Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if we should consider charging more to discourage consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, we need to strike a careful balance between creating an effective behavioural nudge and managing the cost impact on households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The bag charge can be avoided by bringing our own bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We all have to play our part for the environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Shawn Huang asked about the use of proceeds from the bag charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Covered supermarket operators have flexibility to decide on the use of proceeds but will need to account to the public for how they were used.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our approach to mandate annual declarations on the use of proceeds ensures that there is transparency and public accountability, while minimising regulatory and compliance costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I am heartened that all the supermarket operators have indicated that they intend to use the proceeds to support environmental and social causes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Dennis Tan asked about expansion plans for the bag charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will monitor the effectiveness of the bag charge and assess the need to expand coverage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, will we observe new behavioural norms where bringing your own bag for shopping becomes second nature?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Will more retailers follow suit to voluntarily charge for disposable carrier bags?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We can learn from the experience of other jurisdictions such as Hong Kong, Taiwan and England, which have taken a phased approach in extending the coverage of the bag charge over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Don Wee asked if the bag charge would apply to convenience stores.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Convenience stores, such as those operated by Cheers and 7-Eleven that do not sell or prepare raw meats, poultry or seafood, are not required to have supermarket licences and hence, do not come under this legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Nonetheless, I note that Cheers and 7-Eleven are already charging for disposable carrier bags voluntarily.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is because customers do not have the choice of using their own bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Nevertheless, we agree with Ms Carrie Tan that there is scope for online retailers and platforms, not just supermarkets, to reduce packaging waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will study how best to address packaging waste from e-commerce, including online grocery shopping, as we develop the extended producer responsibility scheme for packaging waste management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In the meantime, we will work with the supermarket operators to compile best practices and develop guidelines on reducing packaging for online purchases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We also encourage other retailers to pursue initiatives to reduce and reuse delivery packaging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will monitor the implementation of the bag charge and assess if there is a need to adjust how annual turnover is determined in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On Mr Yip Hon Weng and Ms Joan Pereira's concerns about responsible waste disposal, I would like to reiterate that the practice of properly bagging waste before disposing of it in rubbish chutes should still continue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are not imposing a ban on disposable carrier bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Other packaging such as the bags that hold bread or toilet rolls can also be used to bag waste as alternatives to supermarket carrier bags.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The bag charge should not be an excuse to dispose of waste in an irresponsible manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Don Wee commented that with the bag charge, consumers might start purchasing single-use plastic bags from online and overseas retailers in bulk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: While this is possible, these consumers would likely only buy what they really need and be more mindful of how they use the bags, since they would also have to pay for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Members like Ms Poh Li San and Mr Dennis Tan spoke about the importance of public education to promote greater understanding of the value of sustainability and effect positive behavourial change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our nation-wide "Say YES to Waste Less" campaign has been ongoing since 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As part of the campaign, we work with many partners including supermarkets and F&B establishments to amplify the message of sustainable living and encourage action through initiatives and incentives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The campaign aims to help Singaporeans better appreciate why we need to reduce the use of disposables and food wastage and how to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The campaign messages are shared across multiple touch points and languages to cater to the wider population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government plans to increase public education in conjunction with the commencement of the bag charge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In the lead-up to 3 July, we will ramp up public awareness efforts together with the supermarket operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will remind the public to bring their own bags to avoid the bag charge and offer suggestions on alternatives to supermarket carrier bags for bagging waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are also encouraging the supermarket operators to carry out initiatives to support the transition from disposable to reusable bags, such as bring-your-own-bag initiatives and the distribution of reusable carrier bags, especially to lower-income groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In the spirit of environmental stewardship, I urge everyone to be mindful not to take more disposable bags than necessary and start bringing our own bags, even before the bag charge commences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Gan Thiam Poh have asked about the return point network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Setting up a convenient return point network is a top priority, because it is crucial to the scheme's success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The mandated return points in larger supermarkets will form an important part of the network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At other community spaces and public areas, NEA will work with the scheme operator to encourage premises operators to voluntarily set up return points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Based on the experience overseas, setting up a return point can increase footfall to stores.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The scheme operator will also pay handling fees to return point operators as part of the commercial arrangement, to reimburse costs incurred.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The scheme operator will be setting up return points at locations based on considerations, such as footfall and proximity of return points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The Government will also exercise oversight via licensing conditions to ensure a robust network of return points for the public to return beverage containers conveniently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Don Wee asked about the space taken up by a return point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This would depend on whether the premises operator opts for an over-the-counter return point, or a reverse vending machine (RVM).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Premises operators may work with the scheme operator to determine the optimal RVM size for their premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Don Wee asked whether the scheme operator can exercise creativity in boosting recycling rates, such as by offering supermarket vouchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Return point operators would need to provide a full refund of the deposit amount when the covered beverage container is returned.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: That said, we will certainly encourage the scheme operator to work with stakeholders such as return point operators to explore innovative ways to boost return rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, in addition to the cash option, they could create different options for refund, including supermarket vouchers, rewards points or donation to charity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We see such practices in overseas jurisdictions too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, in Australia, consumers are given the option to donate their refunds directly to charity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond this, return point operators may also work with the scheme operator on further promotional initiatives to increase footfall to their stores, if they wish to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Don Wee asked how the scheme is funded.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is an EPR scheme, where producers are responsible for the collection and recycling of their products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Producers will pay producer fees to the scheme operator to carry out these responsibilities on their behalf.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These fees would be proportional to the beverages they put out to the market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The revenue from the sale of clean, high-quality and high-value recyclables will be utilised by the scheme operator to reduce the scheme costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The eventual cost pass-through to consumers in beverage prices, if any, will likely be moderated by price competition among industry players.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is also the experience in other countries that have implemented similar schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I appreciate that business costs are a concern.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have also heard this feedback at our consultations with companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: At the same time, many have also expressed their support for this scheme, recognising the importance of sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We do need to balance cost and environmental considerations, especially in this uncertain economic environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Therefore, we have taken a consultative and pragmatic approach in developing the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: First, as outlined in my opening speech, we hope to establish an industry-led scheme operator, which is a good practice that we see in jurisdictions overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It will have a strong incentive to operate efficiently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It will also be able to tap on the industry's capabilities and resources to improve operational synergies, such as using existing logistics channels to make backhaul trips.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Second, we will continue to support the industry and provide sufficient time for implementation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In my opening speech, I spoke about how we are adjusting the timeline to implement the scheme based on the industry's feedback.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have also supported the industry with knowledge and capability building.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We organised an industry workshop last year and invited an overseas scheme operator to share best practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to convene and facilitate discussions and knowledge sharing amongst industry stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Third, where possible, we will provide operational flexibility for companies to decide on arrangements that are more cost-effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, producers could consider using stickers for the barcodes and deposit marks, or to directly print them on the beverage container.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Shawn Huang asked about the scenario where the scheme operator fails to meet the return rate target.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: However, we want to avoid this outcome as much as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will support the scheme operator on key scheme aspects that contribute to achieving the return rate, such as public education efforts and deploying a robust return point network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about measures to raise awareness and participation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Indeed, this is a key area of work that we will partner the scheme operator on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will need to reach out to all segments of society, as Mr Yip described, and spread the message in our communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We want to bring everyone on board to do their part for sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Louis Ng and Ms Poh Li San have raised questions and suggestions about the scheme in relation to the broader waste collection industry, including informal waste collectors such as karang gunis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA will work with the scheme operator on appropriate measures to cater to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, the scheme operator could deploy return depots to accept beverage container returns in bulk, similar to arrangements made in other jurisdictions to involve the informal sector in the collection network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Even as we seek to deploy a network of accessible return points to make returning beverage containers as convenient as possible, we recognise that the elderly and less mobile residents may find it more challenging, as Mr Yip Hon Weng highlighted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We want to design a scheme where everyone can participate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to seek out ideas from the community, such as students and community groups, on how we can encourage community support and involvement to make the scheme more accessible to less mobile residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA will work closely with the scheme operator to make the scheme work for these members of our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Including glass bottles or beverage cartons would add complexity and cost to collection logistics and infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: They will continue to be recycled under the National Recycling Programme after the scheme begins.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will monitor the scheme closely and assess the need to expand coverage, if necessary, or to include them in future phases of the wider EPR scheme for packaging.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Shawn Huang asked how the scheme would work for cross-border commercial activities, such as food and beverage services onboard aircrafts and ships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: There are varying circumstances in how the beverages are supplied to aircraft and ships, as well as where the beverage containers are then disposed of.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: NEA has been engaging the industry to develop suitable arrangements for such activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if we would consider requiring other types of buildings, such as SAF cookhouses, schools and hospitals, to segregate food waste for treatment and submit reports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will include SAF cookhouses, schools and public hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Some public sector buildings have already done so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For instance, several polytechnics have introduced food waste segregation measures and installed on-site food waste digesters at F&B areas within their premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For non-public sector buildings, we will explore extending the segregation and reporting requirements to more types of buildings over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Shawn Huang asked about off-site food waste treatment for new buildings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Building managers can determine this based on their business considerations and submit their proposal for NEA's approval.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Our intent is to encourage higher value-added processes, such as valorising food by-products into animal feed ingredients or even food products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: More details on the approval criteria will be provided when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The food waste must be transported by licensed general waste collectors in a manner that safeguards public health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Don Wee suggested that food caterers should take back leftover food from their clients' events for segregation and reporting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: He asked if we would consider imposing penalties on those who dispose of the food waste at the clients' premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: It is primarily the consumers' responsibility to avoid food wastage by ordering just enough food for their guests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We encourage everyone to adopt such sustainable practices to minimise food waste from catering events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Don Wee asked about food waste reporting requirements and frequency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We agree that donating excess food which is safe for consumption will reduce the amount of food waste, and the latter will be reported.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Regarding the Good Samaritan Food Donation Bill, MSE, with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth and the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), will continue to work closely with Mr Ng's team on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked if there is any support provided for community food waste collection and composting solutions to close the food waste loop for households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Under the Green Action for Communities movement, we are hearing good ideas from residents, including on handling food waste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: MSE and Green Plan agencies will work with residents to bring these ideas to fruition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The proposed changes set out in this Bill represent our next steps in this journey towards zero waste and a circular economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In particular, the beverage container return scheme and disposable carrier bag charge will require individuals to adjust their daily lives and their daily habits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Life-as-usual and business-as-usual cannot continue if we are to responsibly steward our resources and environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Each of us has a responsibility to reduce carbon emissions, conserve Semakau Landfill and enhance resource resiliency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: By reducing waste and recycling right, we can do our part to combat climate change and ensure that Singapore remains clean, green and liveable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I call on all Members of the House to give our support to this Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Just one clarification for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I just wanted to ask for the Government's position on the retailers who are not currently covered by this $100 million point.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If they would voluntarily want to impose a plastic bag charge and if, for example, they are going to charge more than what the supermarkets are going to charge, what is the Government's position on this and what is the recourse that Singaporeans may have if they feel that this may come up and this may amount to profiteering or something like that?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For us, we have mandated a low charge of five cents because we are also cognisant of the fact that most people get their disposable bags from the supermarket and if they shop in supermarkets, they tend to require more bags and, if they forget to bring their reusable bags, then they will have to pay for that.
